ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Theoretical Comparison of Randomized Estimators for Shapley Values
PROPOSAL: Analytically compare the expected sample efficiency of KernelSHAP, unbiased KernelSHAP, and LeverageSHAP, derive non-asymptotic bounds for their sample complexities, and discuss their relationships to each other.
CONTROLS: Derive bounds using classical concentration inequalities (e.g., Hoeffding's or Bernoulli inequalities) and compare them with existing asymptotic analyses.
COST: 125
PREDICTION: Expected results will show that, under certain assumptions, LeverageSHAP has the best sample efficiency among the three estimators for a wide range of distributions, while unbiased KernelSHAP has a higher sample complexity due to its perturbation-based construction. However, the practical impact of these differences remains uncertain, especially for the more complex real-world applications.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Sampling Without Replacement for KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effectiveness of sampling without replacement (SWOR) in KernelSHAP, both theoretically and experimentally. Develop and analyze a variant of KernelSHAP that samples row indices randomly subject to a specific probabilistic rule reflecting the SWOR strategy, and study its sample efficiency, accuracy, and robustness to different input distributions.
CONTROLS: Design an experiment where we evaluate the effect of SWOR on KernelSHAP's performance on multiple datasets and model classes. Compare the results with those obtained using paired sampling and full sampling.
COST: 1252.2
PREDICTION: We expect that the proposed variant of KernelSHAP can achieve superior or comparable performance to the original KernelSHAP when paired sampling is not suitable, particularly in large-scale problems or scenarios with correlated data, but may come at a higher computational cost due to maintaining the SWOR rule.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Evaluating Sampling Without Replacement for KernelSHAP (Improved)
PROPOSAL: Refine the previous proposal by incorporating a principled method to adapt the sampling without replacement (SWOR) strategy. Show that dynamic adjustment of the sampling probability according to the recently estimated kernel weights enables Shapley value estimation that efficiently handles changing dependencies in the data, improves robustness against data size, and can adapt to increasingly complex input distributions.
CONTROLS: Theoretical analysis will become based upon the adapted approach, and experiments will involve applying this adaptation to qualitative assessment of its merits on a variety of datasets, demonstrations of inadaptability of Vanilla SWOR-based KernelSHAP, direct comparisons to established algorithms (e.g. LeverageSHAP).
COST: 1600
PREDICTION: We expect that adapting the SWOR strategy will yield significantly improved performance, accuracy, and robustness, surpassing existing algorithms including Vanilla SWOR-based KernelSHAP under diverse data distribution and size scenarios, especially in scenarios with changing correlations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: An Empirical Study of Hyperparameter Sensitivity in Estimators for Shapley Values
PROPOSAL: Investigate the sensitivity of KernelSHAP, LeverageSHAP, and the proposed improved SWOR variant to their hyperparameters, such as the sampling rate, kernel width, and iteration count. Perform a comprehensive hyperparameter tuning on various datasets and models to uncover the optimal choices of hyperparameters and their relative importance. Analyze the observed trends to inform practitioners on how to select the most suitable estimator and hyperparameters.
CONTROLS: We will employ a systematic approach to hyperparameter search using a grid or random search and benchmark several metrics such as mean absolute error, correlation coefficient, and F1-score to evaluate performance. Compare the outcome of improved SWOR variant, also considering results obtained by vanilla methodologies to relate sensitivity of involved estimator.
COST: 3300
PREDICTION: This study should reveal the significant sensitivity of Shapley value estimators to their hyperparameters, indicating that optimal choices largely depend on the specific dataset and model being used. Interestingly, we might find that the proposed improved SWOR variant requires more careful tuning due to the registration of the coordinate descent approach and lack final rounding tolerance heuristic.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Kernel Functions on KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: Investigate how the choice of kernel function in KernelSHAP affects its performance on various datasets and models. Analyze the interplay between the kernel functions and the hyperparameters, and formulate a novel methodology to automatically select the optimal combination of kernel and hyperparameters for a specific problem.
CONTROLS: Use an exhaustive search approach for a smaller scale, and a more efficient distributed search for a larger scale, to investigate the sensitivity of KernelSHAP to the choice of kernel and evaluate its impact on performance using metrics like joint Shapley value and HW Shapley value distances.
COST: 4800
PREDICTION: This study should demonstrate that the choice of kernel function significantly impacts the accuracy of Shapley value estimation and that the ideal kernel/hyperparameter combination depends on the dataset and model. A surprising result might be that an unconventional or bespoke kernel can outperform the typical RBF or polynomial kernels under specific conditions, highlighting the potential for innovation in this area.

ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Kernel Functions on KernelSHAP (Extended)
PROPOSAL: Extend the original proposal by incorporating a novel regularization method for the kernel selection process. The regularization method will aim to penalize overfitting and identify more generalizable kernel combinations that perform well across multiple datasets and models. Empirically evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed regularization approach and compare it to existing methods that solely rely on cross-validation or grid search.
CONTROLS: Regularization approach will be designed to balance the kernel function's complexity and performance on a set of benchmark datasets and models. Experiments will also involve comparison of performance metrics between the regularized approach and existing methods. We will select a blindfolded subset of dataset references.
COST: 6750
PREDICTION: We anticipate that the proposed regularization method will lead to more transferable and robust kernel combinations, reducing overfitting and resulting in improved Shapley value estimation across multiple datasets and models. However, it might come at the cost of slightly reduced performance on very specific problems, highlighting the trade-off between generalizability and adaptability.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adversarial Shapley Value Estimation
PROPOSAL: Design an adversary framework to systematically evaluate the robustness of Shapley value estimators, including KernelSHAP, LeverageSHAP, and the improved SWOR variant. Introduce perturbations to the input data, aiming to reduce the estimator's performance or accuracy, and measure the resilience of each estimator under different types of attacks.
CONTROLS: Use a variety of perturbation methods, such as adversarial examples or causal interventions, to evaluate the robustness of each estimator. Investigate the effects of different perturbation strengths, types, and scopes on the accuracy of Shapley value estimation.
COST: 10183
PREDICTION: We expect that the improved SWOR variant and LeverageSHAP will exhibit better robustness than KernelSHAP under various types of attacks, as they tend to focus less on local linear approximations and more on leveraging global structure. Surprisingly, we might observe that some estimators degrade less than expected under strong attacks, possibly indicating undesired properties like implicit regularization that resolves the issue of estimator instability.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Estimating Higher-Order Shapley Values for Efficient Feature Attribution
PROPOSAL: Develop an efficient algorithm to estimate higher-order Shapley values, which measure the joint contribution of multiple features to model predictions. Introduce a second-order Taylor expansion to approximate the value function, allowing for a reduction in the number of required subset evaluations and improving the scalability of Shapley value estimation for high-dimensional data.
CONTROLS: Develop a set of theoretical bounds on the error of the second-order approximation and experimentally evaluate the proposed algorithm on several real-world datasets, comparing its performance to state-of-the-art methods for computing Shapley values.
COST: 21100
PREDICTION: We anticipate that the proposed algorithm will significantly reduce the computational cost of Shapley value estimation for high-dimensional data while preserving its accuracy and interpretability. However, we might encounter challenges in deriving tight theoretical bounds on the error of the second-order approximation, particularly for non-linear models.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Evaluating Sampling Without Replacement for KernelSHAP (Improved) with a New Optimal Algorithm
PROPOSAL: Revisit the improved sampling without replacement (SWOR) approach for KernelSHAP, aiming to design a more efficient algorithm with a theoretical guarantee on its near-optimality. Introduce a novel method to dynamically adjust the sampling probabilities, leveraging the recent estimates of kernel weights, and explore the convergence properties of the proposed algorithm. We will then compare its performance with the existing methods and provide a set of practical suggestions for its application.
CONTROLS: Derive the mathematical optimization problem of the proposed algorithm and analyze its convergence rate, both theoretically and experimentally. Compare the empirical performance of the proposed algorithm with KernelSHAP and its variants on several benchmark datasets. Analyze its computational efficiency, robustness, and stability on various models.
COST: 28800
PREDICTION: We expect that the proposed improved SWOR algorithm will outperform existing methods for Shapley value estimation, with a faster convergence rate, improved robustness, and enhanced stability. Although achieving near-optimality in practice might come with a relatively higher computational cost, its benefits in terms of accuracy and efficiency will likely outweigh the additional expenses, making it an attractive choice for real-world applications.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Interpreting Model Explanations Using Shapley Values in a Real-World Deployment
PROPOSAL: Develop a comprehensive framework for integrating Shapley value-based explanations into a real-world deployment of a machine learning model. Implement the proposed methods from previous experiments and evaluate their performance on an industrial-scale project. We will report on the practical challenges and successes of using Shapley values to explain predictions in a real-world setting, including a comparison of user acceptance of different explanation methods and their impact on downstream decision-making processes.
CONTROLS: Develop a knowledge graph to collect data on user interactions with the explanations, using it to analyze user acceptance and decision-making outcomes. Collect feedback from subject matter experts to identify potential inaccuracies or ambiguities in the explanations generated by the proposed methods.
COST: 87700
PREDICTION: We anticipate that the proposed framework will facilitate a more transparent and accountable use of machine learning models in real-world applications. While we may face challenges in balancing the computational resources required for Shapley value calculations and the value added by explanations in decision-making, we should be able to demonstrate that users value and rely on the insights provided by these explanations, especially when dealing with critical or high-stakes decisions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comparing Multimodal Fusion Architectures for Temporal Change Description
PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of 4 different multimodal fusion architectures (early fusion, late fusion, attention-based fusion, and temporal convolutional network-based fusion) to generate natural-language descriptions of temporal change in satellite image time series, using the Olivier Vaudrot dataset.
CONTROLS: Naive baseline (textual description only without imagery), separate ablation studies for each fusion method without conditionals (e.g. unaided standard description models),
COST: 43.51
PREDICTION: Attention-based fusion and temporal convolutional network-based fusion may outperform the other two methods, with attention-based achieving 5% higher rouge score on average, but may fail to capture very subtle changes due to overemphasis on high-level features.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring Transfer Learning for Satellite Image Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effect of pre-training a temporal GAN on a large dataset (e.g. DeepShockwave) before fine-tuning on the Targeted Building Extraction dataset, to improve quality and consistency of generated future satellite images.
CONTROLS: Baseline of a non-pre-trained temporal GAN, experimental ablation studies on different pre-training and fine-tuning schedules, 
COST: 84
PREDICTION: Pre-training on a large dataset improves overall forecasting performance by 8 points according to SSIM and PSNR, but may fail to capture fine-grained temporal patterns specific to the Targeted Building Extraction domain.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Temporal Consistency Metrics for Satellite Image Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Develop and evaluate metrics for assessing the temporal consistency of generated satellite image forecasts, including a novel combination of spatial and spectral inconsistencies, using the HRSCEnet dataset.
CONTROLS: Baseline of using standard image quality metrics (PSNR, SSIM) to evaluate forecasting performance, analysis of the impact of changes in individual spectral bands on overall temporal consistency.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: The customized metric outperforms standard image quality metrics in capturing changes between consecutive frames, but may fail to account for changes that occur in ways that are difficult to quantify visually.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Evaluating Temporal Consistency Metrics for Satellite Image Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Develop a quantitative framework that leverages Earth observation-based temporal change indices (TCIs) to assess the temporal consistency of generated forecasts, by integrating TCIs with the customized inconsistency metric introduced in the previous iteration.
CONTROLS: Include baseline experiments using a different Earth observation-based temporal change index, sensitivity analysis of TCI weights on the overall consistency metric.
COST: 180
PREDICTION: Incorporating TCIs improves the ability to detect inconsistencies between consecutive frames by 15% compared to the customized inconsistency metric alone, but may fail to account for effects from exceptional events with large imprecations on the temporal structure.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Temporal Contextualization on MLLMs for Change Description
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effect of adding a temporal contextualization module to an MLLM (e.g., ViLBERT) to capture long-range dependencies in the sequence of satellite images, using the ZY3 dataset for testing.
CONTROLS: Baseline of using an MLLM without temporal contextualization, ablation studies to isolate the contribution of individual components within the temporal contextualization module.
COST: 225
PREDICTION: The temporal contextualization module improves the MLLM's performance by 12% on the change description task, but may fail to handle abrupt changes in the sequence due to its reliance on smoothed temporal features.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Comparing Multimodal Fusion Architectures for Temporal Change Description
PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of the 4 different multimodal fusion architectures with an additional variant that incorporates a generative adversarial network (GAN)-based latent space fusion, to further leverage the strengths of each individual modality.
CONTROLS: Include an ablation study to analyze the impact of the GAN-based fusion on each individual architecture, an investigation of whether the improved performance is due to a better representation of the data or a more effective exploitation of the individual modalities.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: The GAN-based latent space fusion outperforms the other architectures by 18% on average, but may require careful tuning of the hyperparameters to achieve optimal performance, and may suffer from mode collapse in cases where the training data is limited or imbalanced.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Dynamic Hyperparameter Tuning for Improved Forecasting Performance
PROPOSAL: Develop a method to dynamically adjust hyperparameters during training for a temporal forecasting model (e.g., a temporal GAN) to adapt to changes in the underlying temporal structure of the data.
CONTROLS: Implement a baseline method of static hyperparameter tuning, compare performance of dynamic hyperparameter tuning against a variety of competing methods, including random search and Bayesian optimization.
COST: 435
PREDICTION: Dynamic hyperparameter tuning improves the forecasting performance of the temporal GAN by 22% on average, but may lead to overfitting in cases where the changes in the data are too complex or the model is not able to adapt quickly enough.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Evaluating Temporal Consistency Metrics for Satellite Image Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Extend the framework for incorporating Earth observation-based temporal change indices (TCIs) to also account for uncertainty and variability in the TCI estimates themselves, using a probabilistic approach to evaluate the reliability of the temporal consistency metric.
CONTROLS: Include a sensitivity analysis of the probabilistic model parameters on the overall consistency metric, a comparison with a baseline metric that assumes fixed, certain TCI estimates.
COST: 540
PREDICTION: The probabilistic extension to the temporal consistency metric captures the uncertainty and variability in the TCI estimates more accurately, but may require more computational resources and deep expertise in probabilistic modeling, and may suffer from underestimation of uncertainty when dealing with extreme outliers.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Capturing Multi-Scale Temporal Patterns with Hierarchical Residual Modeling
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effect of incorporating a hierarchical residual modeling approach (e.g., hierarchical temporal convolutional networks) into a satellite image time series forecasting model, to adaptively capture multi-scale temporal patterns across different timescales.
CONTROLS: Compare with baseline models using only standard temporal convolutional networks or long short-term memory (LSTM) units, investigate the impact of different hierarchical residual modeling architectures on forecasting performance.
COST: 720
PREDICTION: The hierarchical residual modeling approach improves forecasting performance by 25% on average, but may be computationally expensive and require careful tuning of hyperparameters, and may fail to generalize to unseen datasets or real-world applications due to overfitting to the training domain.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hybrid Approach for Temporal Change Description and Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Develop a hybrid approach that combines the strengths of multimodal fusion architectures and hierarchical residual modeling for satellite image time series forecasting, to effectively capture complex temporal patterns and provide accurate change descriptions and forecasts.
CONTROLS: Compare the hybrid approach with state-of-the-art methods for change description and forecasting, conduct ablation studies to isolate the contribution of individual components and explore the impact of different fusion strategies.
COST: 1008
PREDICTION: The hybrid approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods for both change description and forecasting tasks, but may require substantial computational resources and expertise in model development and optimization, and may suffer from overfitting due to increased model complexity.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Adapter Architectures on Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We compare the performance of different adapter architectures (e.g. 1-layer MLP, 2-layer MLP, convolutional adapter) when updating a pre-trained forecasting model online, using the道路控制 (Road Control) and ELECTRA datasets for traffic flow and electricity transformer temperature forecasting respectively. The adapter architectures will be the controls. For this experiment, the compute estimate is 1222 GPU-hours.
CONTROLS: Comparing 1-layer, 2-layer MLP and convolutional adapters with a frozen base model
COST: 1222
PREDICTION: We expect the 2-layer MLP adapter to outperform the other architectures, as it has been previously shown to be effective in a variety of online learning scenarios; the convolutional adapter may struggle with the localized nature of time series data, while the 1-layer MLP may not have enough capacity to capture complex relationships.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Normalization Strategies in Mitigating Distribution Shift
PROPOSAL: We investigate the impact of different normalization strategies (e.g. layer normalization, instance normalization, learnable normalization) on online time series forecasting, using the M4 dataset for electricity consumption forecasting and the NWS dataset for weather forecasting. The compute estimate is 1831 GPU-hours.
CONTROLS: Comparing performance of forecasting model with different normalization strategies, as well as a baseline model without normalization
COST: 1831
PREDICTION: We expect normalization to improve model robustness to distribution shift, and that learnable normalization will outperform fixed normalization strategies; however, the improvement may be modest, especially if the distribution shift is very rapid.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Batch Sizes on the Performance of Online Gradient Descent
PROPOSAL: We investigate the effect of different batch sizes on the performance of online gradient descent for online time series forecasting, using the Traffic Prediction Challenge dataset and the Solar Forecasting Challenge dataset. We will compare the performance of online gradient descent with different batch sizes (e.g. 1, 5, 10, 20) and also compare it with a baseline model that uses experience replay. The compute estimate is 2700 GPU-hours.
CONTROLS: Comparing performance of online gradient descent with different batch sizes, as well as a baseline model with experience replay
COST: 2700
PREDICTION: We expect that using a larger batch size will reduce the variance of the gradient estimates and improve the performance of online gradient descent; however, this improvement may come at the cost of increased bias due to delayed updates.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Exponential Moving Averages on the Performance of Online Gradient Descent
PROPOSAL: Instead of varying batch sizes, we investigate the effect of different exponential moving averages (EMAs) on the performance of online gradient descent for online time series forecasting, using the same datasets as before. We will compare the performance of online gradient descent with different EMAs (e.g. 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7) and also compare it with a baseline model that uses a naive average. The compute estimate increases to 4350 GPU-hours.
CONTROLS: Comparing performance of online gradient descent with different exponential moving averages, as well as a baseline model with naive average
COST: 4368
PREDICTION: We expect that using an optimal EMA will reduce the variance of the gradient estimates and improve the performance of online gradient descent; the optimal EMA may depend on the specific dataset and forecasting task.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Use of Ensembles for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We investigate the use of ensembles for online time series forecasting, combining the predictions of multiple base models with different architectures and training data. We will use the same datasets as before and compare the performance of different ensemble methods (e.g. bagging, boosting, stacking) and combination strategies (e.g. equal weights, learnable weights). The compute estimate is 6332 GPU-hours.
CONTROLS: Comparing performance of different ensemble methods and combination strategies
COST: 7457
PREDICTION: We expect that ensembling will improve the robustness and accuracy of online time series forecasting, but the optimal ensemble method and combination strategy may depend on the specific dataset and forecasting task.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Concept Drift on Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We simulate concept drift on several real-world datasets (e.g. traffic prediction, electricity consumption) by introducing synthetic changes to the underlying patterns. We will investigate how online time series forecasting models perform in the presence of concept drift and compare the performance of different adaptation strategies (e.g. forgetting mechanisms, adaptive learning rates). The compute estimate is 10800 GPU-hours.
CONTROLS: Comparing performance of different adaptation strategies and online time series forecasting models
COST: 9331.6
PREDICTION: We expect that online time series forecasting models will struggle with concept drift, but that adaptation strategies can improve their performance; the effectiveness of different adaptation strategies may depend on the type and rate of concept drift.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Use of Transfer Learning for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We investigate the use of transfer learning for online time series forecasting, adapting models pre-trained on similar but not identical datasets. We will use the same datasets as before and compare the performance of different transfer learning methods (e.g. fine-tuning, feature learning). The compute estimate is 15300 GPU-hours.
CONTROLS: Comparing performance of different transfer learning methods and online time series forecasting models
COST: 11848.16
PREDICTION: We expect that transfer learning will improve the performance of online time series forecasting models, especially when dealing with concept drift; however, the effectiveness of transfer learning may depend on the similarity between the pre-training and target datasets.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Investigating the Use of Variational Autoencoders for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We investigate the use of variational autoencoders (VAEs) for online time series forecasting, encoding time series data into lower-dimensional representations and decoding them back into forecasts. We will compare the performance of VAE-based models with existing online time series forecasting models and adapter architectures. The compute estimate increases to 21600 GPU-hours.
CONTROLS: Comparing performance of VAE-based models with existing online time series forecasting models and adapter architectures
COST: 16963.76
PREDICTION: We expect that VAEs will capture complex patterns in time series data and improve the performance of online time series forecasting models; however, the effectiveness of VAEs may depend on the dimensionality of the latent space and the chosen architecture.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Use of Graph Neural Networks for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We investigate the use of graph neural networks (GNNs) for online time series forecasting, encoding temporal relationships between time series data as a graph and using GNNs to make predictions. We will compare the performance of GNN-based models with existing online time series forecasting models and adapter architectures. The compute estimate is 32400 GPU-hours.
CONTROLS: Comparing performance of GNN-based models with existing online time series forecasting models and adapter architectures
COST: 22500
PREDICTION: We expect that GNNs will capture complex temporal relationships in time series data and improve the performance of online time series forecasting models; however, the effectiveness of GNNs may depend on the choice of graph structure and the complexity of the temporal relationships.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Theoretical Analysis of Normalization Strategies for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We provide a theoretical analysis of the effect of normalization strategies on the performance of online time series forecasting models, deriving bounds on the convergence rate and regret of different normalization strategies. We will also compare the theoretical results with experimental results from previous proposals. The compute estimate decreases to 8640 GPU-hours, as we no longer need to run experiments to test the normalization strategies.
CONTROLS: Comparison of theoretical results with experimental results from previous proposals
COST: 8640
PREDICTION: We expect that the theoretical analysis will provide insights into the optimal choice of normalization strategy and the conditions under which each strategy is effective.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Effect of a Lightweight Dense Text retriever on Vision-Centric Multimodal Encoders
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the performance of a multimodal retriever that combines a vision-centric ColPali-base encoder with a lightweight dense text retriever, such as the Annoy implementation of FAISS, on visual document retrieval benchmarks likeƯDataset (Ultimate Dataset) and Google's Document Understanding Dataset (GDOUD).
CONTROLS: Compare the combined model with the ColPali-base encoder alone, as well as with a strong baseline of single-vector dense text retriever.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: The combined model will achieve better results than the ColPali-base encoder alone, but may not surpass the strong baseline, possibly because the dense text retriever's signal is not strong enough to compensate for its relative weakness on the task.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Latency-Aware Hybrid Retriever for Multimodal Encoders
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel hybrid retrieval approach that leverages a latency-aware feature fusion technique to combine the outputs of a vision-centric multimodal encoder (e.g., ColPali-base) and a dense text retriever (e.g., Annoy + FAISS) at query time, without requiring knowledge of their internal representations or detailed latency and memory budgets.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed latency-aware hybrid retriever with existing hybrid methods and with the individual encoders, using metrics like recall, precision, and top-k accuracy.
COST: 360
PREDICTION: The proposed latency-aware hybrid retriever will achieve good performance on visual document retrieval benchmarks and will be more efficient in terms of latency and memory usage compared to existing hybrid methods, but may not outperform the individual encoders in some cases.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring Multi-Vector Aggregation Techniques for Combining Heterogeneous Representations
PROPOSAL: Investigate and compare various multi-vector aggregation techniques, such as concatenation, element-wise averaging, and weighting-based fusion, for combining the outputs of a vision-centric multimodal encoder (e.g., ColPali-base) and a dense text retriever (e.g., Annoy + FAISS), which produce different dimensionalities and scales.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the performance of each aggregation technique using metrics like top-k recall, AUC-ROC, and AUC-PR, and compare their robustness to varying dimensionalities and scales of the encoded vectors.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: The concatenation-based approach will likely perform best, but the element-wise averaging method may provide a competitive alternative with lower memory requirements.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Investigating the Effect of a Lightweight Dense Text retriever on Vision-Centric Multimodal Encoders
PROPOSAL: Further investigate the role of training objectives in the fusion of a lightweight dense text retriever and a vision-centric multimodal encoder, comparing retrieval performance under various training objectives, such as retrieval-loss-only, representation-loss-only, and joint retrieval-representation loss.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the combined model under different training objectives using metrics like AUC-ROC and top-k recall, and analyze the representations learned by the combined model to understand the effects of the training objectives.
COST: 776
PREDICTION: The joint retrieval-representation loss will likely provide the best results, but the retrieval-loss-only and representation-loss-only objectives may still achieve competitive performance with fewer training iterations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Impact of Visual-Textual Modality Balance on Multimodal Retrieval
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effect of varying visual-textual modality balance on the performance of the proposed hybrid retriever, using techniques like data augmentation (e.g., text-to-image synthesis) or sample weighting to manipulate the balance between visual and textual modalities in the training data.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the performance of the hybrid retriever under different modality balances using metrics like AUC-ROC and top-k recall, and analyze the learned representations to understand how the balance of modalities influences the retrieval performance.
COST: 720
PREDICTION: The optimal modality balance will depend on the specific dataset and task, but increasing the visual modality balance can often improve performance by exploiting the strength of the vision-centric encoder.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Transferability of Hybrid Retrievers Across Datasets and Tasks
PROPOSAL: Investigate the transferability of the proposed hybrid retriever across different visual document retrieval datasets and tasks, such as image retrieval and question answering on document images, to evaluate its robustness and generalizability.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the hybrid retriever on multiple datasets and tasks using metrics like AUC-ROC and top-k recall, and analyze the transferability of the learned representations to understand how well they generalize across different domains.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: The hybrid retriever will exhibit good transferability across related tasks and datasets, but its performance may degrade on more dissimilar tasks, suggesting the need for adaptability mechanisms to handle domain shifts.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Developing an Adaptive Hybrid Retrieval Framework for Varying Query and Document Lengths
PROPOSAL: Design an adaptive hybrid retrieval framework that can dynamically adjust the contribution of the vision-centric encoder and the dense text retriever based on the length and complexity of the query and document, to optimize retrieval performance under varying conditions.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the performance of the adaptive framework using metrics like AUC-ROC and top-k recall on datasets with documents of varying lengths, and compare its performance to non-adaptive hybrid and single-modal retrieval baselines.
COST: 1008
PREDICTION: The adaptive framework will provide improved retrieval performance under varying conditions, particularly for complex queries and documents, but may incur higher computational costs and require careful tuning of hyperparameters.

ACTION: REVISE 5
TITLE: Investigating Transferability of Hybrid Retrievers Across Datasets and Tasks
PROPOSAL: Extend the analysis of transferability to include not only different datasets and tasks, but also different scales and granularities of visual and textual features, such as comparing the performance of the hybrid retriever on images vs. text documents, and on high-resolution vs. low-resolution images.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the hybrid retriever on various scales and granularities of features using metrics like AUC-ROC and top-k recall, and analyze the transferability of the learned representations to understand how well they generalize across different feature scales and granularities.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: The hybrid retriever will exhibit good transferability across different scales and granularities of features, but its performance may degrade on very high-resolution or low-resolution images, suggesting the need for adaptability mechanisms to handle changes in feature scale.

ACTION: REVISE 6
TITLE: Developing an Adaptive Hybrid Retrieval Framework for Varying Query and Document Lengths
PROPOSAL: Investigate the use of reinforcement learning to optimize the adaptive hybrid retrieval framework, by designing a reward function that encourages the framework to adapt its contribution of the vision-centric encoder and the dense text retriever based on the performance of the retrieval system.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the performance of the adaptive framework using metrics like AUC-ROC and top-k recall on datasets with documents of varying lengths, and compare its performance to non-adaptive hybrid and single-modal retrieval baselines, as well as to reinforcement learning-based adaptive frameworks.
COST: 1400
PREDICTION: The reinforcement learning-based adaptive framework will provide improved retrieval performance under varying conditions, particularly for complex queries and documents, and will be able to adapt to changing conditions more effectively than non-adaptive frameworks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Large-Scale Evaluation of Hybrid Multimodal Retrieval on Visual Document Datasets
PROPOSAL: Design a large-scale evaluation protocol to compare the performance of the proposed hybrid multimodal retrievers with state-of-the-art single-modal and multimodal retrieval systems on multiple visual document datasets, and analyze the results to understand the strengths and limitations of each approach.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the hybrid retrievers with state-of-the-art single-modal and multimodal retrieval systems using metrics like AUC-ROC, top-k recall, and mean average precision (MAP), and analyze the results to understand the effectiveness of each approach on various visual document datasets.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: The large-scale evaluation will provide valuable insights into the strengths and limitations of hybrid multimodal retrieval, and will help to identify potential areas for improvement and future research directions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Parallel Reasoning Traces Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune a language model on a set of diverse, correct reasoning traces per question generated by a teacher model, and evaluate its ability to retain distinct reasoning modes and trigger them reliably when sampling in parallel.
